content.canonical: A winning ticket discovered on CIFAR-10a (a subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset containing 25,000 training images with 2,500 images per class), transfers to a disjoint subset CIFAR-10b from the same data distribution and improves training on that held-out subset relative to random sparse initializations.

The within-distribution transfer described in claim 12 holds for both VGG19 and ResNet50. [Referenced claim 12: A winning ticket discovered on CIFAR-10a (a subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset containing 25,000 training images with 2,500 images per class), transfers to a disjoint subset CIFAR-10b from the same data distribution and improves training on that held-out subset relative to random sparse initializations.]
ResNet50 showed sensitivity at low pruning fractions, occasionally under-performing random tickets when few weights are pruned.

On CIFAR-10b with ResNet50, at extreme pruning fractions, both types of winning tickets—those produced on CIFAR-10a and those produced on CIFAR-10b—achieve better performance than random tickets; the error bars correspond to mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

On CIFAR-10b with ResNet50, at low pruning fractions, both types of winning tickets—those produced on CIFAR-10a and those produced on CIFAR-10b—achieve worse performance than random tickets; the error bars correspond to mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

When CIFAR-10 is divided into 10a and 10b, each consisting of 25,000 training images (2,500 per class), winning tickets produced on CIFAR-10a generalize effectively to CIFAR-10b for VGG19 and ResNet50; the error bars correspond to mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

For ResNet50 models evaluated on CIFAR-10b, winning tickets generated from both CIFAR-10a and CIFAR-10b outperformed random tickets at extreme pruning fractions, with error bars representing mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

For ResNet50 models evaluated on CIFAR-10b, winning tickets generated from both CIFAR-10a and CIFAR-10b underperformed random tickets at low pruning fractions, with error bars representing mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

In the CIFAR-10 split into 10a and 10b halves, each containing 25,000 training images (2,500 per class), winning tickets generated using CIFAR-10a generalized well to CIFAR-10b for both VGG19 and ResNet50, with error bars representing mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.
